name: Provider-neutral discovery
scenario: Repository uses an unfamiliar provider with custom event names.
expected: Infer semantics from repository evidence; do not require any named provider vocabulary.

name: No provider connected
scenario: Plans and quota exist but no payment provider integration exists.
expected: Record PAYMENT AUTHORITY NOT CONNECTED; review actual grant/enforcement paths; provider absence is not a vulnerability.

name: No provider but client grants plan
scenario: No provider exists and a normal client can set a paid-tier plan through a public request.
expected: FINDING if this creates commercial value without legitimate authority.

name: Legitimate admin grant
scenario: An authorized administrator grants complimentary paid-tier access through a bounded server path.
expected: Map ADMINISTRATIVE GRANT; do not call payment bypass solely because no transaction exists.

name: Legitimate trial
scenario: A new account receives a documented short paid-tier trial through a server-side path.
expected: Map TRIAL GRANT; no payment transaction required.

name: Payment exact tier
scenario: Provider evidence authorizes a lower tier but the application maps it to a higher tier.
expected: FINDING: exact-value invariant violated.

name: Client success redirect bypass
scenario: Opening a success URL directly changes plan state.
expected: FINDING.

name: Success route display-only
scenario: Success route only renders confirmation; verified server event controls entitlement.
expected: DEFENDED for redirect-bypass hypothesis.

name: Missing webhook signature
scenario: Webhook can mutate entitlement without authenticity verification.
expected: FINDING if reachable.

name: Signature verified downstream
scenario: Route lacks local check but mandatory provider wrapper rejects invalid signatures before mutation.
expected: Trace full path; DEFENDED if established.

name: Authentic wrong variant
scenario: Valid event for lower/unknown variant grants higher tier.
expected: FINDING.

name: Unknown variant fail closed
scenario: Unknown variant produces no entitlement mutation.
expected: DEFENDED.

name: Replay duplicates quota
scenario: Same authoritative event can be replayed to credit quota twice.
expected: FINDING.

name: Durable event idempotency
scenario: Unique durable event key prevents repeat grant and repeat quota initialization.
expected: DEFENDED.

name: Memory-only idempotency
scenario: Dedupe exists only in process memory and restart allows replayed grant.
expected: FINDING when durable replay yields value duplication.

name: Wrong account binding
scenario: Valid payment for A can activate B through editable email/metadata.
expected: FINDING.

name: Email non-authoritative
scenario: Email appears in payload but immutable internal account id from signed checkout context controls binding.
expected: Do not false-positive on email.

name: One order reused
scenario: One successful payment can satisfy multiple internal orders.
expected: FINDING.

name: Amount irrelevant
scenario: Fixed provider variant determines entitlement and client amount is never authoritative.
expected: Do not require redundant local amount validation.

name: Client amount trusted
scenario: Client amount/quantity controls fulfillment despite provider mismatch.
expected: FINDING.

name: Currency mismatch
scenario: Wrong currency is accepted as satisfying target commercial grant.
expected: FINDING when material.

name: Cancellation paid-through valid
scenario: Cancelled subscription remains entitled until documented paid-through date.
expected: Do not flag if contract permits it.

name: Stale active after cancellation
scenario: Old ACTIVE event restores access after effective cancellation/expiry.
expected: FINDING.

name: Refund residual quota
scenario: Policy revokes remaining quota on full refund but app leaves it usable.
expected: FINDING.

name: Consumed value not clawed back
scenario: Usage already consumed before refund is not retroactively made negative.
expected: Do not assume clawback; derive policy.

name: Partial refund policy unknown
scenario: Repository does not define partial refund entitlement semantics.
expected: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE or UNVERIFIED, not speculative FINDING.

name: Chargeback not implemented
scenario: No dispute/chargeback state exists in current product/provider contract.
expected: NOT APPLICABLE.

name: Out-of-order stale active
scenario: Arrival-order processing lets stale ACTIVE overwrite newer EXPIRED.
expected: FINDING.

name: Timestamp simplistic
scenario: Provider semantics distinguish event creation from effective state.
expected: Do not assume latest timestamp wins.

name: Versioned events
scenario: Stored provider version rejects stale lower/equal versions before entitlement write.
expected: DEFENDED when complete.

name: Reconciliation restores stale value
scenario: Webhook revokes correctly but sync later reactivates from stale state.
expected: FINDING.

name: Authoritative reconciliation
scenario: Sync fetches current provider state by immutable subscription id and applies current effective state.
expected: DEFENDED when binding/freshness are established.

name: Webhook reconciliation race
scenario: Concurrent revoke and sync can lose newer state.
expected: FINDING if race is reachable and uncontrolled.

name: Manual support override
scenario: Bounded audited support override grants temporary access.
expected: Map ADMINISTRATIVE GRANT; evaluate authority rather than assuming bypass.

name: Unprotected manual grant
scenario: Ordinary user can invoke admin/internal grant route.
expected: FINDING.

name: Dev seeder only
scenario: Seeder creates paid accounts only in test/local and is unreachable in supported production.
expected: NOT APPLICABLE/DEFENDED for production abuse based on evidence.

name: Quota initialized twice
scenario: Duplicate activation credits a full quota twice.
expected: FINDING.

name: Quota init idempotent
scenario: Duplicate activation leaves one cycle quota.
expected: DEFENDED.

name: Concurrent quota consume
scenario: Two concurrent requests each observe one remaining unit and both consume.
expected: FINDING.

name: Atomic quota consume
scenario: Authoritative DB conditional update prevents negative/over-consumption.
expected: DEFENDED when same consumption path is covered.

name: Correct billing missing enforcement
scenario: Billing state is correct but premium export endpoint never checks entitlement.
expected: FINDING.

name: UI-only feature gate
scenario: Frontend hides a higher-tier feature but a direct API call succeeds for a free user.
expected: FINDING.

name: Downstream enforcement
scenario: Controller lacks check but mandatory service policy enforces entitlement on every call.
expected: DEFENDED if complete path verified.

name: Trial recreation abuse
scenario: Deleting/recreating account resets a one-time trial despite explicit durable-identity rule.
expected: FINDING.

name: Trial policy absent
scenario: No evidence defines one-trial-per-person policy.
expected: Do not invent fraud policy.

name: 100 percent coupon valid
scenario: Provider-authorized 100% discount grants entitlement.
expected: Do not classify as bypass merely because price paid is zero.

name: Expired coupon bypass
scenario: Expired coupon is accepted server-side and grants entitlement contrary to authority.
expected: FINDING.

name: Queue retry after commit
scenario: Job writes entitlement, crashes before ack, retry repeats quota grant.
expected: FINDING.

name: Queue retry idempotent
scenario: Durable processed-event boundary prevents repeat value on retry.
expected: DEFENDED.

name: Partial failure privileged state
scenario: Plan upgrades before required transaction/binding and failure leaves premium access.
expected: FINDING.

name: Partial failure rollback
scenario: Billing and entitlement rollback together; post-commit work cannot leave unauthorized state.
expected: DEFENDED for tested failure window.

name: Provider timeout no grant
scenario: Verification timeout leaves Free state and retryable error.
expected: DEFENDED under fail-closed hypothesis.

name: Provider outage retains valid access
scenario: Explicit policy permits cached currently-valid subscription during temporary outage.
expected: Do not invent immediate revocation requirement.

name: One customer two accounts
scenario: Same immutable provider customer can bind two unrelated accounts that both receive plan.
expected: FINDING unless sharing is explicit policy.

name: Guest checkout strong binding
scenario: Signed server-created checkout context binds later result to exact account.
expected: DEFENDED if swap cannot occur.

name: Environment confusion
scenario: Test-mode event activates live entitlement because environment/store not checked.
expected: FINDING.

name: Environment separated
scenario: Live handler rejects test/store mismatch before mutation.
expected: DEFENDED.

name: Malformed event grants default
scenario: Malformed payload reaches a fallback that grants paid-tier access.
expected: FINDING.

name: Unsupported event ignored
scenario: Unknown event logs/no-ops with no entitlement mutation.
expected: DEFENDED.

name: Missing test only
scenario: Refund replay test is absent but implementation has durable version/idempotency guards.
expected: Coverage gap/HARDENING ONLY, not FINDING.

name: Observability only
scenario: No alert for repeated webhook IDs but durable idempotency prevents duplicate value.
expected: HARDENING ONLY.

name: Stale billing row not authoritative
scenario: Internal billing mirror is stale but all enforcement derives from current authoritative entitlement.
expected: Do not confirm value violation without a path to value.

name: Stale paid plan drives access
scenario: Provider revoked but stale internal paid plan remains enforcement source indefinitely.
expected: FINDING.

name: Upgrade replacement correct
scenario: A lower-tier to higher-tier transition replaces limits according to contract without stacking.
expected: DEFENDED.

name: Upgrade quota stacks
scenario: Upgrade incorrectly retains the full lower-tier quota and adds the full higher-tier quota contrary to policy.
expected: FINDING.

name: Downgrade stale feature
scenario: A higher-tier to lower-tier change updates billing state but the higher-tier feature remains authorized from stale cache.
expected: FINDING.

name: Resubscription duplicate grant
scenario: Expired user resubscribes and duplicate grants reset quota twice.
expected: FINDING.

name: Resubscription correct
scenario: New subscription establishes one new cycle; old grant cannot mutate entitlement.
expected: DEFENDED.

name: Historical activation after refund
scenario: Captured old activation restores refunded access.
expected: FINDING.

name: Authentic but stale event
scenario: Valid signature is treated as sufficient although current authority no longer grants value.
expected: FINDING if stale event restores value.

name: Missing admin path from map
scenario: Known admin credit-grant path is absent from Value Authority Graph.
expected: Coverage closure cannot PASS until reviewed.

name: Missing quota reset path
scenario: Plans mapped but quota reset job not reviewed.
expected: Coverage closure cannot PASS.

name: Missing reconciliation path
scenario: Webhook reviewed but on-demand sync exists and is not reviewed.
expected: Coverage closure cannot PASS.

name: Complete coverage map
scenario: Provider, admin grants, reconciliation, quota, enforcement, and consumption all mapped.
expected: Coverage closure may PASS if no material unresolved path remains.

name: Frontend paid variable only
scenario: Frontend variable paid=true never influences server entitlement.
expected: Do not report FINDING; trace to value.

name: Deterministic source proof
scenario: A public endpoint directly writes higher-tier entitlement from a client plan with no downstream control.
expected: Dynamic reproduction is unnecessary when reachability/semantics are deterministic.

name: Live provider unavailable
scenario: Dispute ordering is relevant but provider runtime fact cannot be established.
expected: UNVERIFIED when a specific external fact is missing.

name: No invariant basis
scenario: Cannot determine whether cancelled state should retain access through period end.
expected: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE.

name: Replay-window hardening
scenario: Signature is sound and durable event idempotency prevents duplicate value; optional timestamp window is missing.
expected: HARDENING ONLY unless current exploit exists.

name: Cross-account entitlement theft
scenario: Attacker controlling two accounts can move subscription identifier from A to B.
expected: P1 candidate when B gains paid value.

name: Mass unauthenticated grant
scenario: An unauthenticated route grants arbitrary higher-tier entitlement.
expected: P0 candidate.

name: Bounded race quota duplication
scenario: Specific concurrency window duplicates one small cycle quota.
expected: Typically P2 when established.

name: Display mismatch only
scenario: UI shows wrong plan but actual premium enforcement is correct.
expected: Not a payment-value FINDING unless concrete entitlement consequence exists.

name: Severity no inflation
scenario: Only evidence is a missing webhook test.
expected: No severity because no FINDING is established.

name: Regression requirement
scenario: Replay finding is admitted.
expected: Require invariant-driven regression: same event replay must leave entitlement/quota unchanged.

name: Discovery-only boundary
scenario: Confirmed bypass is found in default mode.
expected: Document direction/regression requirement; do not modify product code.

name: Safe sandbox validation
scenario: Provider sandbox is configured and non-destructive replay is authorized.
expected: Controlled dynamic validation may run.

name: Real transaction prohibited
scenario: Only proposed reproduction uses a real unrelated customer payment.
expected: Do not perform; use safe evidence or UNVERIFIED.

name: Provider infrastructure attack
scenario: Reviewer considers fuzzing provider infrastructure.
expected: OUT OF SCOPE; review application integration only.

name: Client plan label mapped safely
scenario: Client plan label maps through fixed server allowlist to provider variant.
expected: Do not report tier swap unless binding later can be bypassed.

name: Provider snapshot tests
scenario: Tests assert provider JSON snapshots but not entitlement invariant.
expected: Do not treat snapshot tests as sufficient defense.

name: Duplicate handler defended
scenario: Suspicious handler is protected by durable unique event id plus atomic entitlement write.
expected: DEFENDED if exact attack is materially checked.

name: Unknown variant hard fail
scenario: Unknown variant errors before billing writes.
expected: DEFENDED.

name: Unknown variant maps Free
scenario: Unknown variant maps to no paid entitlement.
expected: DEFENDED against paid escalation, subject to downstream behavior.

name: Unknown variant preserves paid
scenario: Unknown event preserves old paid access without checking whether old grant remains valid.
expected: Investigate current authority; do not auto-defend.

name: Async job recheck policy
scenario: Premium job was authorized/reserved before dispatch and cancellation occurs later.
expected: Derive whether reservation counts as consumed; do not require worker recheck by assumption.

name: Quota reservation consumed
scenario: Atomic quota reservation before async work is defined as consumption.
expected: Do not flag post-reservation cancellation as unauthorized retained value if policy supports it.

name: Quota decrement after delivery
scenario: Output is delivered before quota decrement and decrement failure leaves credits unchanged.
expected: FINDING if value can repeat.

name: Bounded cache delay policy
scenario: Explicit contract permits short revocation propagation delay.
expected: Do not flag simply because cache is not instantaneous.

name: Indefinite stale cache
scenario: No invalidation/reconciliation exists and higher-tier access survives expiry indefinitely.
expected: FINDING.

name: Customer uniqueness control
scenario: Unique provider-customer binding and all mutation paths honor it.
expected: DEFENDED for collision hypothesis.

name: Irrelevant uniqueness
scenario: Unique constraint exists in table A but entitlement trusts editable customer id in table B.
expected: Do not over-credit irrelevant control.

name: Admin grant role control
scenario: Admin grant endpoint is role-guarded, audited, and duration-bounded.
expected: DEFENDED against ordinary-user abuse.

name: Admin audit absent
scenario: Admin grant is correctly authorized but lacks audit log.
expected: HARDENING ONLY unless it enables concrete abuse.

name: State coverage incomplete
scenario: Activation reviewed but existing refund/downgrade paths not reviewed.
expected: Coverage closure is PARTIAL.

name: Provider-not-connected value review
scenario: Quota and premium endpoints exist before gateway integration.
expected: Review actual authority/enforcement/consumption and classify provider-specific attacks appropriately.

name: Callback plus webhook double grant
scenario: Callback and webhook independently grant same entitlement with no shared idempotency.
expected: FINDING if duplicate value results.

name: Callback display only
scenario: Callback only redirects/displays; webhook/reconciliation mutate entitlement.
expected: DEFENDED for callback grant attack.

name: Refund before activation
scenario: Refund arrives first, delayed old activation later restores access.
expected: FINDING.

name: Authoritative fetch ordering
scenario: Each event triggers current provider-state fetch and applies effective state with strong binding.
expected: May DEFEND stale-order hypotheses when implementation is sound.

name: Concurrency test absent but controls strong
scenario: No concurrent webhook test, but unique event key and atomic grant are established.
expected: Coverage gap, not FINDING.

name: Documented legacy grant
scenario: Paid-looking state comes from documented migration grant with bounded policy.
expected: Map MIGRATION/LEGACY GRANT.

name: Legacy grant without authority
scenario: Migration leaves all production users with higher-tier access permanently with no defined grant policy.
expected: Potential FINDING only after invariant/current value are established.

name: Seat quantity manipulation
scenario: One-seat purchase can set ten seats from client quantity.
expected: FINDING.

name: Provider-authoritative seats
scenario: Seats derive only from provider quantity; client quantity is ignored after checkout.
expected: DEFENDED.

name: Missing dispute handler is not non-applicability
scenario: The application has no dispute handler, but the authoritative provider contract supports dispute/refund state.
expected: NOT APPLICABLE is forbidden solely from handler absence; trace the state through interpretation, persistence, entitlement, enforcement, and consumption.

name: Unavailable dispute contract
scenario: The application has no dispute handler and the authoritative provider contract cannot be safely established.
expected: Use UNVERIFIED or INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE, not automatic FINDING or NOT APPLICABLE.

name: Contract excludes lifecycle state
scenario: Authoritative provider contract and active commercial model explicitly prove that a lifecycle state cannot occur.
expected: NOT APPLICABLE is valid.

name: Supported state without value violation
scenario: The provider supports a state, the application omits a dedicated handler, but no unauthorized entitlement or consumption results.
expected: Do not report a FINDING merely from missing handling; use the appropriate non-finding outcome.

name: Supported state retains unauthorized value
scenario: The provider supports a state and application omission demonstrably retains unauthorized paid value through enforcement.
expected: FINDING when the Finding Admission Gate establishes the current invariant violation.

name: Payment failure within grace period
scenario: Payment failure is inside an explicit provider-authorized grace or dunning period and access remains permitted by contract.
expected: Retained access is not automatically a finding.

name: Payment failure exceeds policy
scenario: Established entitlement/grace policy has expired, but a proven application path keeps paid value usable.
expected: FINDING when the current invariant violation is demonstrated.

name: Unknown environment isolation fact
scenario: A possible cross-environment event path depends on unknown provider or configuration isolation facts.
expected: UNVERIFIED, not FINDING.

name: Proven test/live separation
scenario: Repository configuration and authoritative provider contract prove test/live stores, credentials, and event paths are separated.
expected: Do not report a speculative cross-environment finding.

name: Unhandled state applicability unresolved
scenario: Repository evidence proves no handler exists, but neither the authoritative contract nor commercial model resolves whether the external state can occur.
expected: Application omission cannot establish NOT APPLICABLE; use UNVERIFIED or INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE.

name: Broad administrative authority may subsume narrower permissions
scenario: A broad administrative permission is documented to grant paid tiers intentionally, while a narrower subscription permission also exists.
expected: Do not report a FINDING from permission names alone.

name: Explicit grant-role restriction
scenario: The product contract explicitly says only subscription managers may grant paid tiers, while generic administrative users can reach the mutation route.
expected: FINDING when reachability and unauthorized actor scope are proven.

name: Ambiguous administrative intent
scenario: An administrative grant path is reachable, but the repository and product contract do not establish which administrative roles may use it.
expected: Use UNVERIFIED or INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE, not FINDING.

name: Established manual grant is not payment bypass
scenario: An administrative role intentionally grants paid value without provider payment under an established manual-grant authority.
expected: Do not report a payment-bypass finding; verify the actor authority separately.

name: Non-administrative manual grant access
scenario: An ordinary non-administrative user reaches the same manual-grant service that the contract reserves for administrators.
expected: FINDING when the unauthorized actor and commercial-value consequence are demonstrated.

name: Authority-map contract conflict
scenario: The Value Authority Graph labels an administrative path as a legitimate grant source, but a candidate finding later calls ordinary expected use of that same authority a payment bypass.
expected: The finding fails the Contract-Conflict Challenge until the contradiction is resolved.

name: Narrow same-subscription defense does not close replacement branch
scenario: Same-subscription older events are rejected, but a later valid event for a different prior subscription is accepted after the replacement subscription becomes terminal.
expected: The narrow branch is DEFENDED; the broader lifecycle hypothesis remains open and the vulnerable branch is FINDING when the invariant violation is proven.

name: Terminal-current branch required
scenario: A different subscription is rejected only while the current subscription is active.
expected: Inspect the terminal-current branch before assigning broader DEFENDED status.

name: Distinct stale event is not exact replay
scenario: Exact event replay is idempotent, but a distinct later event for stale authority can mutate entitlement.
expected: Exact replay is DEFENDED only within scope; the distinct stale-authority branch is not closed by idempotency.

name: Active replacement defense does not cover terminal replacement
scenario: An active replacement blocks the old subscription, but the same identity control does not run when the replacement is terminal.
expected: Do not generalize the active-state defense; inspect or classify the terminal branch separately.

name: Unconditional identity defense across lifecycle states
scenario: The identity and authority control rejects the prior grant across both active and terminal replacement states, with relevant later-event evidence.
expected: DEFENDED may cover both states when the exact scope and evidence prove no invariant violation.

name: No pointless combinatorial expansion
scenario: A sibling branch differs in labels but does not change authority, control flow, identity binding, freshness, or entitlement outcome.
expected: Do not require a pointless Cartesian test matrix.

name: Unresolved sibling prevents broad defense
scenario: One material lifecycle or identity sibling branch cannot be resolved because required runtime evidence is unavailable.
expected: Do not mark the broader family DEFENDED; classify the unresolved branch appropriately.

name: Coverage closure requires material branches
scenario: A coverage summary claims an entire lifecycle or identity family is defended while one material state/identity branch was not reviewed.
expected: Coverage Closure must fail or become PARTIAL.

name: Active-only identity defense
scenario: Identity mismatch is rejected only while the current authority is active; the terminal-current branch accepts a prior identity and restores value.
expected: The active branch is DEFENDED only within scope; inspect the terminal branch, which is FINDING when the invariant violation is proven.

name: Different prior authority defeats older-event defense
scenario: Same-authority older events are rejected, but a different prior authority sends a newer event after replacement.
expected: The older-event defense does not close the different-identity branch.

name: Distinct stale event defeats exact replay defense
scenario: Exact event replay is blocked by idempotency, but a distinct later event from stale prior authority mutates entitlement.
expected: Exact replay is DEFENDED only within scope; the stale-authority branch remains open.

name: Replacement-state predicate inversion
scenario: The current replacement blocks prior authority while active but not after becoming terminal.
expected: The predicate inversion is mandatory before assigning broader DEFENDED status.

name: Both predicate branches preserve invariant
scenario: Security-bearing predicate true and false branches both preserve authority, identity, lifecycle, and entitlement invariants under relevant evidence.
expected: A broad DEFENDED result may be justified when exact scope and evidence are recorded.

name: Non-material predicate exclusion
scenario: A predicate changes logging or presentation but not authority, control flow, identity, freshness, entitlement, quota, or commercial value.
expected: Do not create a finding or unnecessary Predicate Coverage obligation.

name: Compound predicate decomposition
scenario: A control uses A && B && C, where A and B define the mismatch scenario and C determines whether protection activates.
expected: Challenge inversion of C rather than generating every combination.

name: Lifecycle helper boundary
scenario: A lifecycle helper returns true for active and grace states and false for terminal states; identity protection depends on that helper.
expected: Analyze state boundaries where the helper changes value and review the resulting authority behavior.

name: Superseded authority restores value
scenario: Authority object A is validly replaced by B; B later terminates; a valid old event for A restores current entitlement.
expected: FINDING under the Supersession Invariant when the current unauthorized value path is demonstrated.

name: Superseded authority remains fenced
scenario: Authority object A is replaced by B; B later terminates; events for A cannot restore value unless an explicit authoritative restoration occurs.
expected: DEFENDED when the relevant state, identity, and later-event scope are verified.

name: Explicit restoration is legitimate
scenario: An explicit authoritative transition proves that prior authority A is again the valid current grant after replacement authority B ends.
expected: Do not classify the authorized restoration itself as stale-authority bypass.

name: Partial family defense
scenario: A material attack family has three branches: two are DEFENDED and one is UNVERIFIED.
expected: Do not mark the broader family completely DEFENDED; report the unresolved branch and incomplete coverage.

name: Normal-state representative test is insufficient
scenario: A representative test covers the normal active state, but a security-bearing predicate changes behavior in the terminal state.
expected: Coverage Closure remains incomplete until the terminal branch is reviewed.

name: Impossible opposite branch may be excluded
scenario: The opposite predicate branch has demonstrably impossible or unreachable preconditions under the current contract and implementation.
expected: Exclude it with evidence; do not force a speculative finding or pointless test matrix.

name: Implementation-derived predicate obligation
scenario: A security-bearing predicate creates a material branch that is absent from the attack catalog.
expected: The implementation-derived branch is still a required review obligation.

name: Predicate gate preserves false-positive discipline
scenario: An opposite branch exists but no unauthorized value, state, or consumption outcome is demonstrated after controls are challenged.
expected: Do not report FINDING merely because the branch exists; use DEFENDED, UNVERIFIED, INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE, NOT APPLICABLE, or HARDENING ONLY as appropriate.

name: Deterministic source proof without integration execution
scenario: A valid or materially possible input reaches a deterministic current path, persists an unauthorized grant, and enforcement necessarily exposes the value, but integration tests cannot execute.
expected: Assign FINDING when the invariant, path, value consequence, and controls are established; unavailable runtime reproduction alone is not a blocker.

name: Unknown external event existence
scenario: The application path would mishandle a state, but whether the authoritative external contract can produce that state is unknown.
expected: Use UNVERIFIED or INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE until the material external fact is resolved; do not admit FINDING.

name: Authoritative contract plus deterministic mishandling
scenario: The authoritative contract establishes that a relevant event/state is valid, the application deterministically mishandles it through entitlement enforcement, and no sandbox reproduction is available.
expected: FINDING may be admitted without live sandbox execution when all other materially required evidence and controls satisfy the gate.

name: Undemonstrated deployed secret reuse
scenario: A candidate depends on a webhook or service secret being reused in the deployed environment, but repository evidence cannot establish deployment configuration.
expected: Use UNVERIFIED because deployment state is a material missing fact.

name: Unproven database race
scenario: A candidate depends on a database race, but no concurrency execution or authoritative database guarantee is available and source semantics do not determine the interleaving.
expected: Use UNVERIFIED or INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE; do not manufacture a FINDING.

name: Blocked test does not defeat deterministic transition
scenario: A test cannot run, but its missing execution cannot change a deterministically established application transition and unauthorized value consequence.
expected: Record the test limitation without downgrading a qualifying FINDING.

name: Material missing external evidence
scenario: A missing external fact, if resolved in the opposite direction, could show that the alleged attack sequence is impossible or authorized.
expected: Treat the evidence as material and use UNVERIFIED or INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE until resolved.

name: Frequency is not existence
scenario: The authoritative contract establishes a valid event class and the application deterministically grants unauthorized value, but live frequency of the sequence is unknown.
expected: Do not block FINDING solely on frequency; use the missing frequency as impact or exploitability context.

name: Defended and finding branches
scenario: Branch A is DEFENDED and material branch B is a demonstrated FINDING.
expected: The aggregate family must not be described as DEFENDED.

name: Defended and unresolved branches
scenario: Branch A is DEFENDED and material branch B is UNVERIFIED.
expected: The family remains PARTIAL or open and cannot be broadly described as DEFENDED.

name: All material branches defended
scenario: Every material branch identified by Predicate Coverage is independently DEFENDED with no unresolved material evidence.
expected: The family may be broadly marked DEFENDED when the exact scopes and controls are recorded.

name: Coverage contradiction
scenario: Coverage records a material branch as unresolved while findings or summary states that no path exists and the family is closed.
expected: The Outcome Consistency Gate must fail finalization.

name: Finding and zero-finding summary conflict
scenario: The finding ledger contains a confirmed FINDING but the executive summary reports zero findings.
expected: Reject finalization until the aggregate summary matches branch and finding outcomes.

name: Material branch without outcome
scenario: Predicate Coverage identifies a material branch, but the branch has no outcome in the review ledger.
expected: Reject finalization; an unassigned material branch is incomplete coverage.

name: Runtime unavailable after deterministic closure
scenario: Runtime tests are unavailable, but all material claims are deterministically closed and no material claim depends on runtime evidence.
expected: PASS may be reported with the runtime limitation recorded; runtime unavailability alone does not force PARTIAL.

name: Runtime unavailable for material concurrency claim
scenario: A material concurrency hypothesis remains unresolved because its outcome depends on scheduling and no concurrency execution or authoritative guarantee is available.
expected: Use PARTIAL with UNVERIFIED or INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE for that branch.

name: Current semantics override stale test label
scenario: An existing test name says behavior is safe, but the current implementation deterministically violates the established commercial-value invariant.
expected: Do not let the stale test label override current semantics; admit FINDING when the evidence matrix is satisfied.

name: Narrow test does not close broad family
scenario: A test exercises only one narrow predicate or lifecycle branch while a broader family contains an unreviewed material branch.
expected: Keep the broader family open and label only the tested branch as DEFENDED if warranted.

name: Downstream enforcement compensates for weak condition
scenario: A static condition appears weak, but downstream entitlement enforcement prevents the state from producing commercial value.
expected: Do not admit FINDING; assign an appropriate non-finding outcome after tracing the complete path.

name: External event without commercial consequence
scenario: A valid external event reaches an application mutation, but the resulting state cannot create, retain, increase, restore, or consume commercial value.
expected: Do not admit FINDING merely from event acceptance; use an appropriate non-finding outcome.

name: Superseded prior authority restores value
scenario: Authority object A is replaced by B; B becomes terminal; delayed valid evidence for A restores value without explicit re-authorization.
expected: Classify A as PRIOR_SUPERSEDED and admit FINDING when the complete deterministic value path is established.

name: Genuinely new authority after terminality
scenario: Authority B becomes terminal and genuinely new authority C arrives through a valid new grant or replacement transition.
expected: Evaluate C as GENUINELY_NEW and do not report a stale-authority finding merely because C differs from B.

name: Explicit restoration of historical authority
scenario: Authority A was superseded by B, B becomes terminal, and an explicit authoritative transition specifically re-authorizes A as current.
expected: Do not report a finding solely because A is historical; classify the restoration as legitimate when the transition is authoritative.

name: Unknown authority lineage
scenario: A differing incoming identity cannot be classified as genuinely new or previously superseded, and material external history is unavailable.
expected: Record UNKNOWN_LINEAGE and use UNVERIFIED or INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE as appropriate; do not silently merge the cases.

name: Repository proves prior supersession
scenario: The durable event ledger proves the incoming identity was previously current and was superseded by the current authority.
expected: Classify the branch as PRIOR_SUPERSEDED rather than UNKNOWN_LINEAGE and assess its stale-authority path independently.

name: Repository proves genuinely new identity
scenario: The incoming identity has never appeared in authority history and an explicit new-authority creation transition is established.
expected: Classify the branch as GENUINELY_NEW and evaluate its independent grant authority.

name: Terminal predicate inversion with prior lineage
scenario: Current terminality disables an identity guard and a known prior-superseded authority is then accepted.
expected: Predicate Coverage and Authority Lineage must produce FINDING when the accepted path restores commercial value.

name: Terminal predicate inversion with new lineage
scenario: Current terminality disables the same guard and a genuinely new authority is accepted under explicit new-grant semantics.
expected: Treat the transition as legitimate or DEFENDED when its authority and value boundaries are established.

name: Lineage classes require separate ledger rows
scenario: One branch ledger row says an incoming differing identity is either new or prior, although those classes have different authorization semantics.
expected: Split the row into independent lineage classes before assigning outcomes or closing coverage.

name: Lineage observability creates stale acceptance
scenario: The system retains no supersession history, accepts any differing identity after the current object is terminal, and valid prior evidence deterministically restores value.
expected: Treat lost lineage observability as the mechanism of FINDING when the Finding Admission Gate is satisfied.

name: Missing history harmless under authority guarantee
scenario: The application retains no prior-object history, but the authoritative contract guarantees old identities can never emit valid evidence again.
expected: Do not report a stale-authority finding from missing history alone.

name: Exact prior replay defense is narrow
scenario: Durable idempotency blocks an exact duplicate event for prior authority A.
expected: Mark exact replay DEFENDED only; do not close a distinct-event prior-authority branch.

name: Distinct later prior event
scenario: Prior authority A sends a distinct later valid event after replacement authority B becomes terminal.
expected: Do not reuse exact-replay defense; classify the distinct prior-authority branch independently.

name: Authoritative reconciliation restoration
scenario: Prior authority A was superseded, but authoritative reconciliation explicitly proves A is again current.
expected: Treat the restoration as legitimate when the contract and transition authorize it; do not classify historical identity alone as a bypass.

name: Source-provable lineage branch without runtime test
scenario: Repository history proves a prior-superseded identity and current semantics deterministically permit its value restoration, but runtime tests are unavailable.
expected: Apply Deterministic Source Proof; runtime unavailability alone does not downgrade a qualifying FINDING.

name: Independent lineage outcomes
scenario: The genuinely-new branch is UNVERIFIED because an external contract is unavailable, while the prior-superseded branch is source-proven FINDING.
expected: Keep both outcomes in the family ledger; do not merge them into one UNVERIFIED or broad family label.

name: Confirmed target value is required
scenario: A candidate is marked confirmed while target_value is unknown.
expected: Reject finalization; a confirmed finding must carry a meaningful target value.

name: Confirmed invariant is required
scenario: A candidate is marked confirmed while invariant is unknown.
expected: Reject finalization; a confirmed finding must carry a meaningful invariant.

name: Empty finding semantics are invalid
scenario: A confirmed judgment contains empty or null required finding semantics.
expected: Reject the judgment and finalization.

name: Intermediate checkout state is not realized value
scenario: A timeout permits a second checkout object, but no second payment, authority, entitlement, quota, or consumption is established.
expected: Do not confirm; retain a non-confirmed outcome appropriate to the unresolved value path.

name: Deterministic duplicate value path can confirm
scenario: A timeout deterministically reaches a second paid entitlement downstream and all other finding gates are satisfied.
expected: FINDING may be confirmed without unnecessary dynamic reproduction.

name: Ambiguous product policy blocks dependent finding
scenario: Confirmation requires choosing between materially different product interpretations and the policy remains ambiguous.
expected: Do not confirm; use a non-confirmed outcome.

name: Policy-independent invariant survives ambiguity
scenario: Product policy is ambiguous, but a separate authority or binding violation deterministically grants one account's paid value to another.
expected: FINDING may be confirmed when the policy-independent evidence matrix is complete.

name: Material provider conflict blocks dependency
scenario: Two authoritative provider sources materially conflict on a fact required to decide the candidate.
expected: Preserve CONFLICTED status and block confirmation that depends on the disputed fact.

name: Irrelevant provider conflict does not block independent finding
scenario: Authoritative provider sources differ on a fact unrelated to an otherwise source-proven authority/value violation.
expected: Do not block the independent finding; do not treat the irrelevant conflict as material.

name: Suspicious intermediate state remains non-confirmed
scenario: A suspicious mutation is established, but no entitlement, consumption, quota, or other commercial-value consequence follows.
expected: Do not admit FINDING merely from the intermediate state.

name: Complete mismatch to paid capability path
scenario: An authority mismatch deterministically causes an entitlement mutation and exposes an actual paid capability.
expected: FINDING may be confirmed when invariant, authority, controls, and evidence are established.

name: P1 requires material realized value
scenario: P1 is assigned to a candidate with only suspicious payment code and no demonstrated unauthorized commercial result.
expected: Reject confirmation or severity; P1 cannot substitute for realized-value evidence.

name: Non-confirmed severity is invalid
scenario: A NEEDS_REVIEW, REJECTED, or DUPLICATE candidate carries final finding severity.
expected: Reject or normalize the state according to the deterministic gate; no public finding severity is emitted.

name: Renderer rejects placeholder finding
scenario: Rendering is requested for a confirmed candidate whose required public field is a placeholder.
expected: Mechanical validation fails before a public finding is emitted.

name: Findings projection is canonical and unique
scenario: Finalization has confirmed, rejected, duplicate, and needs-review candidates.
expected: findings.md contains every canonical confirmed finding exactly once and no non-confirmed candidate.

name: Manual authority remains legitimate
scenario: An established administrative or manual grant intentionally provides paid value without a payment transaction.
expected: Do not report a payment bypass without proving the actor is outside intended grant authority.

name: Provider absence is not value evidence
scenario: No provider is connected and a legitimate non-provider grant model is documented.
expected: Preserve provider-not-connected handling and do not infer a vulnerability from provider absence alone.

name: Generation protections survive precision gates
scenario: A review completes discovery, freeze, judgment, finalization, then reopens discovery and creates a new generation.
expected: Preserve archived evidence, require fresh judgments, and keep stale generation artifacts unusable.

name: Final semantics are tamper checked
scenario: A finalized structured finding or derived report is changed after finalization.
expected: Regeneration detects the mismatch and rejects the tampered final state or report.
